concept: A cracked flange passes machine-vision inspection beside a 95% accuracy display. Represents the article's missed-defect example without Persian text.
prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: premium editorial cover for an article titled "What does 95 percent accuracy mean for a factory?" Wide landscape 16:9 composition, high resolution.
Primary request: Make a concrete, immediately understandable factory quality-inspection scene that exposes how an impressive accuracy percentage can conceal missed defects. A striking professional magazine cover photograph, not an abstract AI illustration and not a diagram.
Scene: a plausible industrial machine-vision inspection station in a real metal-parts factory. Foreground has a conveyor with several machined steel flanges, satin metal, oily fingerprints, realistic fine machining marks. One large flange closest to the viewer has an unmistakable deep radial crack running from the central hole across the metal face toward the edge. It is structurally defective, not merely scratched. The cracked flange has already passed the camera and continues down the accepted conveyor. A small physically mounted green inspection status display beside this part says "PASS" with a green check mark, clearly contrasting with the visible defect. No green marking is painted on the actual part.
Behind it, a compact industrial inspection camera with a ring light is mounted above the conveyor. On the side of the same machine, a believable angled industrial monitor displays the exact two-line text "95%" and "ACCURACY" in large clean pale typography; below, a small green check. Its screen is simple and legible, with no fake charts or extra statistics. The monitor is a real physical screen in the scene, not a floating hologram.
Composition: tightly composed hero image with the cracked metal part and the readable 95% monitor as the two dominant focal points. Three-quarter camera viewpoint near conveyor height, natural perspective. Enough view of the camera and factory in the softly blurred background to identify industrial inspection immediately. The crack must remain conspicuous at thumbnail size. Protect the key elements inside the central 80 percent for responsive cropping. Do not add a headline over the image.
Style: cinematic but credible industrial editorial photography, tactile steel and rubber, controlled cool neutral factory light with warm amber accents, green only for the misleading pass status. Moderate depth of field with both the important foreground crack and the monitor readable. Strong composition, restrained, sophisticated, real-world engineering equipment.
Text permitted ONLY: "95%", "ACCURACY", "PASS". Require exact spelling. Absolutely no Persian or Arabic text, no other writing, no logos, no brand names, no watermark, no humanoid robot, no brain icon, no neon circuitry, no sci-fi elements. No explosive damage or sparks. This is an illustrative scene, not a claim to document a real factory.
